newsitem.title: UK: UK houses selling faster, near asking price - report.
newsitem.headline: UK houses selling faster, near asking price - report.

text.p: British houses on average are being sold 16 weeks after coming onto the market on average and at 94 percent of the asking price, according to a report by estate agents Black Horse Agencies, part of Lloyds Bank.
That means houses are now selling five weeks faster, on average, than they were in June, the report said, and 25 percent of properties are being sold within six weeks.
The agency said a combination of falling UK unemployment, stable interest rates and better house prices were stimulating the market.
"Properties are selling, and they are selling fast," said David Wood, managing director of Black Horse Agencies.
The report said a house put on the property market in August 1995 for 100,000 stg would have sold for 92,000 stg on average. Now it would fetch 94,000 stg.
"As demand gets stronger across the country and property prices improve, more and more people who have had their property on the market for a while will find selling easier," Wood said.
